description: Four original, source-linked organ guide additions. Distinguishes modern anatomy, historical esoteric attribution, planetary symbolism, unverified historical therapeutics, research gaps. Supersensible origins not inserted where source evidence is lacking.

guides.title: The lungs
guides.subtitle: Breath · rhythm · outer world
guides.one_liner: Steiner discusses the lungs through breath, heart–lung rhythm, air/sound formation, inner-Mercury imagery and claims about memory and future form.
guides.intro: Breathing is the anchor, but Steiner's different contexts must stay separate: the actual lungs exchange gases, while his air/sound, planetary and future-organ descriptions are historical esoteric interpretations.

quick_takeaways.title: The chest works as a system
quick_takeaways.body: Steiner's medical lectures place lungs alongside the heart in a wider rhythmic, etheric organization.

quick_takeaways.title: Formative air is not the same as elemental earth
quick_takeaways.body: A 1924 discussion emphasizes air/sound organ formation, while GA 205 assigns the lung an earth-element affinity in another kind of map.

quick_takeaways.title: Mercury is an analogy
quick_takeaways.body: GA 128 provisionally refers to the lung system as inner Mercury; that does not establish its physical origin or an exclusive spiritual builder.

body.note: Lungs lie in the thorax around the heart and allow oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange. Modern respiratory physiology is distinct from Steiner's proposed spiritual explanation of breathing, organ shape or epilepsy.

cards.title: Where and what they do
cards.body: The two lungs expand during breathing and exchange respiratory gases with blood. This is general modern anatomical orientation.

cards.title: Breath and rhythm
cards.body: The medical lectures interpret lung/heart activity within a chest-wide rhythmic and etheric interplay, rather than as isolated organs.

cards.title: Formative interplay
cards.body: In GA 314, Steiner attributes lung form to an interplay of imagined kidney–liver radial activity and head-rounded forces.

interpretation.intro: Steiner uses different explanatory languages for the lungs—etheric organization, formative sound/air, spiritual memory and outer-world polarity. These are not experimentally established lung functions.

cards.title: Heart–lung etheric account
cards.body: The paired organs are discussed as a rhythmic process involving the etheric organization.

cards.title: Air and sound forces
cards.body: A 1924 medical lecture proposes organ-forming activity involving air and sound, with the lungs comparatively close to those processes.

cards.title: Surface and interior images
cards.body: GA 205 associates lung surfaces with abstract-thought memory and the interior with the future outer head, as spiritual-life imagery.

cards.title: Mercury, not literal astronomy
cards.body: GA 128 names a supposed inner-Mercury correspondence for the lung system.

evolution.lead: The evidence does not supply a complete, sourced lung-by-lung chronology through every cosmic embodiment. Below are different temporal or relationship contexts, not a continuous clinical timeline.

timeline.title: Air enters an early respiratory process
timeline.body: GA 102 associates the arrival of air during Earth's recapitulation with early respiratory conditions; it does not describe a fully developed present lung.

timeline.title: Air and sound organization
timeline.body: GA 316 gives the lungs a comparatively close relation to air/sound-forming forces; the passage is not a dated planetary genesis claim.

timeline.title: Rhythm, breath and head–metabolic polarity
timeline.body: GA 313/314 discuss the chest's present interlocking rhythmic activity.

timeline.title: Lung interior and later head form
timeline.body: GA 205 connects inner lung forces with the appearance of a future head in a karmic interpretation.

compare.conclusion: Air as a formative medium and earth as a symbolic elemental correspondence are different categories, not a source contradiction about physical gas exchange.

agencies.intro: The indexed passages do not identify a single hierarchy as the exclusive creator or maintainer of the lungs. The human etheric, astral and I members are not names of independent angelic ranks.

rows.agent: No unique named lung-builder in this selection
rows.target: Lung formation in an organ-process account
rows.caveat: A claim about forces is not proof of an exclusive being responsible for the organ.
The member is a category of organization, not a named hierarchy.

rows.target: Lung in a disputed curative-education theory
rows.caveat: The associated explanation of seizures/consciousness is medically unsupported and must not be used for diagnosis.

connections.intro: Each node is a separate documented kind of relationship. Select it to open the original lecture context.

nodes.label: Earth element
nodes.detail: The elemental earth affinity is distinct from the air/sound formation account.

questions.title: Which hierarchies actually act upon the lungs?
questions.body: The selected first-pass passages name formative processes, but do not justify a unique builder or a completed agency timeline.

questions.title: Why air in one lecture and earth in another?
questions.body: The lectures use air/sound as attributed formative forces and earth as an elemental correspondence. The scope and genre must be annotated separately.

questions.title: What about Steiner's epilepsy account?
questions.body: GA 317 links seizures and altered consciousness to organ-bound astral/I processes. This explanation is not supported by modern neurology, and medical decisions should not use it.

questions.title: What remains to be checked?
questions.body: A complete bilingual audit of organ genesis, German wording of major source cues, and comparison across other lectures remain pending.

guides.title: The brain
guides.subtitle: Head · thinking · organismic polarity
guides.one_liner: Steiner relates the brain and head to sensory life, thinking, the human I and several distinct cosmic or developmental interpretations.
guides.intro: His account alternates between the physical brain, the head as a broader organization, a spiritual theory of thought, and symbolic correspondences. The Atlas keeps those targets distinct.

quick_takeaways.title: Head is not the whole nerve-sense system
quick_takeaways.body: GA 313 places nerve-sense activity especially in the head, while saying the wider activity extends throughout the body.

quick_takeaways.title: The brain as a thought mirror is Steiner's claim
quick_takeaways.body: GA 317 proposes that the brain reflects preexisting world-ether thoughts into ordinary mental images. This is not an established neuroscience theory.

quick_takeaways.title: Formative contexts are multiple
quick_takeaways.body: GA 128 proposes older brain/spinal-cord force history; GA 102 associates the forebrain with I-related development. Neither alone yields a complete cosmic chronology.

body.note: The brain lies in the skull and is the central organ for neural information processing, perception, movement, cognition and bodily regulation. The anatomical brain is not identical to Steiner's whole-head or etheric-astral conceptual categories.

cards.title: A protected physical organ
cards.body: Brain and spinal cord form the central nervous system and are protected by skull and vertebral structures.

cards.title: Head and sensory organization
cards.body: Steiner's threefold account centers nerve-sense organization in the head, yet does not restrict it solely to the skull.

cards.title: Brain and spinal cord imagery
cards.body: GA 128 describes the brain as a transformed spinal-cord-like formation within his evolutionary force account; this is not a modern anatomical phylogeny.

interpretation.intro: The primary texts distinguish the human I, astral and etheric organization from the physical brain. These are spiritual-scientific assertions, not independently demonstrated neural mechanisms.

cards.title: Head as an imprint
cards.body: GA 313 presents the head as bearing an imprint of I, astral and etheric organization while physical forces are emphasized.

cards.title: Warmth and light ether
cards.body: A subsequent lecture claims that the head is relatively open to warmth and light ether compared with chemical and life ether.

cards.title: The brain as a reflecting instrument
cards.body: GA 317 says the brain and nerves reflect world-ether thoughts; it also offers an unvalidated breakdown theory of neural tissue.

cards.title: Forebrain and I activity
cards.body: GA 102 describes the forebrain as an expression of the I's work upon the astral organization across incarnational development.

evolution.lead: These stages concern whole cosmic evolution, individual incarnations and present cognition. No claim is made that a modern brain existed in its current form on Old Moon.

timeline.title: Wisdom imprint, not modern cortex
timeline.body: GA 102 attributes traces of wisdom in bone, heart and brain to Old Moon group-soul activity; it is not an isolated anatomical brain-origin statement.

timeline.title: I activity and the forebrain
timeline.body: Steiner describes the forebrain in terms of the I acting on astral organization across life development.

timeline.title: Nerve-sense and the thought mirror
timeline.body: GA 110/317 give present brain-mediated consciousness a distinct role, with GA 317's world-ether theory remaining spiritual speculation.

timeline.title: Connections from organs to later brain qualities
timeline.body: GA 205 links liver interiors to a supposed future inner brain disposition, rather than to a verified organ-growth mechanism.

left.label: Old Moon setting
left.detail: Attributed wisdom imprint on multiple organs

compare.conclusion: An Old Moon wisdom-imprint claim and a successive-incarnation I-account refer to different temporal and causal contexts.

agencies.intro: Named group souls, human constitutional members and ordinary bodily organization must not be represented as one homogeneous list of organ-building spiritual hierarchies.

rows.caveat: This does not establish an exclusive named builder for the modern brain.
The human I is not a named separate hierarchy.
Head organization is not identical to the physical brain alone.

connections.intro: An individual edge may link the brain, the wider head, or another system. Read its scoped text and source before inferring a causal equivalence.

nodes.label: The I
nodes.detail: GA 102 presents the forebrain as related to the I acting on astral organization.

nodes.label: Nerve-sense
nodes.detail: GA 313 locates nerve-sense processes especially in the head but also throughout the body.

nodes.label: Spinal cord
nodes.detail: GA 128 imagines an older brain-forming history through a transformed spinal cord.

nodes.label: Liver
nodes.detail: GA 128 connects a forebrain region and liver through an inner tin/Jupiter correspondence; GA 205 also offers a future-life image.

nodes.label: Spleen
nodes.detail: GA 128 links posterior head and spleen via lead/Saturn correspondences.

questions.title: Brain or whole head?
questions.body: Many passages concern the head/nerve-sense system, not a discrete anatomical brain function. Each source must preserve its actual target.

questions.title: How literal is the thought-mirror account?
questions.body: GA 317 attributes thought to a world-ether process and nerves to breakdown; these are historically significant but unvalidated by neuroscience.

questions.title: Who did what in Old Moon evolution?
questions.body: The GA 102 group-soul image requires staged, cross-lecture German examination; it does not identify one exclusive modern-brain maker.

questions.title: What is still incomplete?
questions.body: Additional lectures, exact organ-versus-system targeting, independent review and comprehensive original-German collation remain outstanding.

guides.title: The kidneys
guides.subtitle: Filtration · astral interpretation · inner Venus
guides.one_liner: Steiner associates kidney activity with respiratory–digestive balance, astral organization, a Venus analogy and future temperament images.
guides.intro: This guide separates actual renal excretion from Steiner's spiritual correspondences, claims about childhood head processes and historical treatments.

quick_takeaways.title: A balancing theory
quick_takeaways.body: GA 128 assigns kidneys an unconscious harmonization of respiration and digestion as well as removal of excess products.

quick_takeaways.title: Venus is a label of correspondence
quick_takeaways.body: In GA 128 the kidney force-system is provisionally termed inner Venus; that is not an account of anatomical origin on the present planet.

quick_takeaways.title: Astral and head relations differ
quick_takeaways.body: GA 314 associates the kidney system with astral processes and with childhood head reflections; the passage does not certify an organ-specific hierarchy builder.

body.note: The kidneys are paired organs high in the posterior abdomen, not directly illustrated in the Atlas's current frontal medical plate. They filter blood, regulate fluid/electrolyte balance and produce urine. These are modern physiological functions, unlike the historical spiritual theories below.

cards.title: Not pictured on this front view
cards.body: The kidneys lie toward the back of the upper abdomen, one on either side of the spine. Their functions include filtration and regulation of fluid, electrolytes and blood pressure.

cards.title: Renal activity and bodily poles
cards.body: Steiner assigns kidneys a harmonizing role between digestive and respiratory processes in GA 128.

cards.title: Physical organ and force system
cards.body: Steiner distinguishes the physically secretory kidney from attributed etheric and astral force-processes in GA 128.

interpretation.intro: Steiner's claims about astral kidney forces, psychological dispositions and treatments must be read as historical spiritual-scientific interpretations, not proven nephrology or psychiatry.

cards.title: Astral organization
cards.body: GA 314 places the kidney system into relation with the astral organization.

cards.title: Venus correspondence
cards.body: GA 128 provisionally calls the kidney system an inner Venus and later places it in a Venus/copper analogy.

cards.title: Children and the head
cards.body: GA 314 describes kidney–astral activity being reflected through the developing head.

cards.title: Temperament image
cards.body: GA 205 links renal processes to allegedly lasting emotional habits and future head disposition.

evolution.lead: Kidney-specific first origins on Old Saturn, Old Sun or Old Moon have not been established by the selected citations; Venus is a correspondence, not a planetary-building stage.

timeline.title: Specific organ rudiment unestablished
timeline.body: The current selected passages do not give a verified claim of the kidneys' first creation by a named hierarchy on a particular cosmic embodiment.

timeline.title: Inner Venus
timeline.body: GA 128 uses Venus terminology as a present organ-force correspondence, not the chronological birth of the kidneys.

timeline.title: Astral–head reflection
timeline.body: GA 314 gives an interpretation connecting the kidney/astral organization to childhood head development.

timeline.title: Emotional temperament
timeline.body: GA 205 links the inner kidney system with the disposition of future temperament.

compare.conclusion: Inner Venus and an air-element association do not identify one literal cosmic origin or a proven physical process.

agencies.intro: An astral organization, an esoteric planetary analogy and a named hierarchy are distinct kinds of reference. No unique kidney-building angelic rank is established here.

rows.target: Kidney system and the developing head
rows.caveat: A human constituent member is not an exclusive named hierarchy.
Do not turn inner Venus into the name of a spiritual builder.
Not demonstrated as effective treatment; not a recommended medical intervention.

connections.intro: These are different relational categories; clicking a node reveals the exact source rather than an unqualified one-to-one equivalence.

questions.title: What is the actual cosmic origin?
questions.body: No complete first-rudiment history or exclusive named hierarchy builder has been established in the selected ledger; do not fill this gap from the Venus analogy.

questions.title: How do Venus and air relate?
questions.body: The planetary Venus label in GA 128 and the air-element relation in GA 205 come from different symbolic frameworks.

questions.title: Are the medical interventions effective?
questions.body: GA 315 proposes vowel/consonant movement effects on kidney function and urination; such claims are not established treatments. GA 128 also contains unsafe historical metal-vapor ideas.

questions.title: What remains to be verified?
questions.body: Full German text and broader cross-corpus comparison, plus claim-by-claim actor identification, remain pending.

guides.title: The spleen
guides.subtitle: Rhythm · nourishment · inner Saturn
guides.one_liner: In GA 128 Steiner assigns the spleen a mediating role between irregular meals and blood rhythms and treats its physical and supersensible aspects as distinct.
guides.intro: The existing dossier is less developed than the Heart, Liver, Brain or Lungs. This is a deliberately bounded GA 128 guide with five closely related passages—not a complete account of spleen origins or spiritual builders.

quick_takeaways.title: Meals and rhythm
quick_takeaways.body: GA 128 III portrays a supposed splenic rhythm as mediating between irregular dietary timing and blood activity.

quick_takeaways.title: Saturn is a qualified analogy
quick_takeaways.body: GA 128 II provisionally calls the spleen an inner Saturn; that is not a claim that it first formed on Old Saturn.

quick_takeaways.title: Physical vs. supersensible spleen
quick_takeaways.body: GA 128 IV–V explicitly separates the anatomical spleen from what Steiner calls a persistent supersensible force system.

body.note: The spleen is normally located in the upper left abdomen near the stomach, mostly beneath the ribs. It filters blood and performs important immune functions. It is not separately visible in the current frontal illustration, so no misleading hotspot is placed over another structure.

cards.title: Position and modern role
cards.body: The spleen is in the left upper abdomen and participates in immune surveillance, blood filtering and red-cell recycling. This is modern anatomical orientation.

cards.title: Food rhythm in Steiner's account
cards.body: GA 128 III gives the spleen an alleged mediation between food intake and circulating blood rhythm.

cards.title: Physical tissue versus force image
cards.body: GA 128 V argues for a supersensible pattern expressed through the physical spleen, a claim not validated by physiology.

interpretation.intro: The splenic teachings indexed here are concentrated in GA 128. They describe a spiritual-force system, a Saturn analogy and alleged dietary and blood-rhythm relationships.

cards.title: Rhythmic light image
cards.body: Steiner portrays the inwardly perceived spleen as a luminous rhythm whose expansion and contraction relate to meals.

cards.title: Inner Saturn
cards.body: The splenic force process is provisionally linked to Saturn-like self-regulation. It is a correspondence, not organ creation on the celestial planet.

cards.title: Persistence after removal
cards.body: Steiner claims the supposed splenic supersensible activity might remain after splenectomy, while explicitly warning against transferring this assertion to every organ.

cards.title: Spleen and head analogy
cards.body: GA 128 VIII connects posterior head/occiput with spleen through lead–Saturn symbolism.

evolution.lead: This dossier's selected material does not establish an organ-specific Old Saturn-to-Earth creation sequence. 'Inner Saturn' is symbolic terminology, not evidence of physical splenic genesis.

timeline.title: No unique first-rudiment claim certified
timeline.body: The GA 128 material selected here does not identify the precise first evolutionary condition or a named group of beings that exclusively built the spleen.

timeline.title: Provisional inner Saturn
timeline.body: GA 128 II uses Saturn as a label for the spleen's alleged inner-world force relation, not a developmental date.

timeline.title: Meal and blood rhythms
timeline.body: GA 128 III attributes a moderating role to the splenic force system in the discrepancy between eating and blood processes.

timeline.title: Physical spleen versus enduring process
timeline.body: GA 128 IV–V describes a hypothetical splenic force organization that does not necessarily end when the organ is removed.

right.label: Old Saturn embodiment
right.detail: No first-rudiment claim established in this selected dossier

compare.conclusion: The same planetary word must not be mistaken for proof that a modern organ originated in the corresponding cosmic embodiment.

agencies.intro: The passages distinguish an alleged formative force system, the physical organ and dietary rhythms. They do not establish a single named builder of the spleen.

rows.caveat: Saturn is a conceptual analogy here, not a hierarchy.
Supersensible bodies are theoretical anthroposophical members, not established anatomic components.
A dietary behavior is not itself a spiritual being.

connections.intro: These five links use concepts already indexed in GA 128 and should be read as separate metaphysical or functional assertions.

nodes.label: Meals
nodes.detail: An alleged splenic rhythm is said to compensate for irregular meal times.

nodes.label: Blood
nodes.detail: Steiner relates the splenic rhythmic light-image to the rhythmic activity of blood.

nodes.label: Saturn
nodes.detail: The splenic system is called inner Saturn as a provisional analogy.

nodes.label: Liver–gall
nodes.detail: Steiner discusses spleen with liver and gall in ascending nutritive processes.

nodes.label: Occiput
nodes.detail: An esoteric lead/Saturn mapping links posterior head and spleen.

questions.title: Is inner Saturn the Old Saturn origin?
questions.body: No such inference is supported: a provisional correspondence in GA 128 is not the same predicate as a cosmic first-rudiment narrative.

questions.title: Does a force system survive surgical removal?
questions.body: Steiner makes that spiritual claim in GA 128, but it is not demonstrated physiology, and the passage does not provide medical advice about splenectomy.

questions.title: Which beings shaped the spleen?
questions.body: The current dossier has no exclusive named hierarchy assignment; stronger claims would require independent primary-source audit.

questions.title: What is missing?
questions.body: A broader GA 313–317 cross-audit for spleen-specific claims, stage-by-stage evolution, German comparison and organ-specific medical context remain unfinished.
